overview.text:
Coimbatore — known to almost everyone as Kovai — is Tamil Nadu's second-largest city and one of its great working centres. Its textile mills earned it the name Manchester of South India, and today it is also a hub for engineering, education, IT and healthcare.

The region was once known as Kongunadu, ruled in turn by local chieftains, the Cholas and later dynasties up to the Vijayanagara empire. For travellers, its value is its position: it lies near the Palghat Gap, with the Western Ghats rising on the horizon, and it makes a natural stopover for the Nilgiris, Valparai and the Anamalai hills. The airport at Peelamedu is about 15 km from the city centre. The weather is mildest from November to March, the best time to visit.

places.summary: A quiet tea town at 3,500 ft in the Anamalai hills — hornbills, lion-tailed macaques and waterfalls.

places.seoDescription: Valparai: tea and coffee estates at 3,500 ft in the Anamalai hills, lion-tailed macaques, hornbills, Aliyar dam and Monkey Falls.

overview.text:
Valparai is a small, quiet hill town at about 3,500 ft on the Anamalai range of the Western Ghats. The drive up is half the adventure, climbing hairpin bends through forest, and at the top the hills open out into tea plantations and coffee estates hemmed in by forest.

This is one of the best places in Tamil Nadu for wildlife. The Indira Gandhi Wildlife Sanctuary is home to lion-tailed macaques, barking deer and wild boar; the range is also a habitat of the Nilgiri tahr, and great, Malabar pied and grey hornbills are often seen. Around the town are the Upper Sholayar, Nirar and Aliyar dams, Monkey Falls and the forest path to Chinnakallar falls. Coimbatore airport is about 119 km away and Pollachi station about 64 km.

places.summary: Tiger and elephant forest in the Nilgiris, linked to Bandipur and Wayanad — a tiger reserve since 2007.
places.seoTitle: Mudumalai National Park and Tiger Reserve
places.seoDescription: Mudumalai: 321 sq km of Nilgiri forest bordering Bandipur and Wayanad; tiger reserve since 2007, 266+ bird species, a key elephant corridor.

overview.text:
Mudumalai National Park covers 321 sq km of forest on the slopes of the Nilgiris, at 850–1,250 m, where Tamil Nadu meets Karnataka and Kerala. It joins Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary to the west and Bandipur National Park to the north, so together they form one great sweep of wild country.

That continuity matters most for elephants: Mudumalai and the neighbouring Sigur forest give the region's Asian elephants their best-connected range. The park was declared a tiger reserve in 2007, and records at least 266 bird species and 18 species of carnivore. Most of its rain falls in the southwest monsoon, from June to September. Drive slowly on the public roads through the park — traffic is a real danger to wildlife here.

overview.text:
Coonoor is the second-largest hill station in the Nilgiris, wrapped in tea plantations that are often clouded in mist. It is a place to slow down: walk the estates, find the waterfalls in the valleys and look out from its many viewpoints.

In town, Sim's Park — named after J D Sim, a former government secretary — is full of unusual plants and shrubs and good for birds such as bulbuls, babblers and robins; it also hosts an annual fruit and vegetable show. Further out are Lamb's Rock, Dolphin's Nose, Catherine and Law's falls and the old Droog Fort. Don't miss the Nilgiri train ride from Coonoor up to Ooty. Coimbatore airport is about 71 km away, and October to March is the best time to come.

places.name: Tiruchirappalli (Trichy)
places.summary: Old Chola city on the Kaveri — the Rockfort, Srirangam's vast temple and Jambukeswarar.
places.seoDescription: Trichy: Chola city on the Kaveri with the Rockfort, Srirangam's Ranganathaswamy Temple and Jambukeswarar; airport 5 km from the city.

overview.text:
Tiruchirappalli — Trichy for short — is one of the oldest cities in Tamil Nadu. It stands on the banks of the Kaveri, where it was the citadel of the Early Cholas, and its landmark, the Rockfort, has its roots in the reign of the Pallava king Mahendravarman I.

Most visitors come for the temples. Just north of the city, on an island in the river, Srirangam's Ranganathaswamy Temple is one of the largest temple complexes in the world; the Jambukeswarar Temple, to Shiva, and the Samayapuram Mariamman Temple are also important. For shopping, the government-run Poompuhar emporium sells bronzes, Thanjavur paintings and handwoven textiles. The international airport is only 5 km from the city, and Trichy Junction has direct trains to Chennai, Bengaluru, Mumbai and Delhi.

places.summary: Trichy's landmark — a temple on a great rock, 437 steps up, with views over the city and Srirangam.
places.seoDescription: Trichy's Rockfort: the Uchippillaiyar temple on a Pallava-carved rock, 437 steps up, with views of Srirangam. 3 km from Trichy Junction.

overview.text:
The Rockfort is Tiruchirappalli's landmark: a huge outcrop of rock rising from the middle of the city, crowned by the Uchippillaiyar temple to Ganesha. The ancient Pallavas first carved the rock, and the Nayaks of Madurai and the Vijayanagara empire later expanded and renovated the temples here, mixing their styles.

The climb is the experience. Some 437 steps, many cut into the rock, lead up past carved walls and shrines to the top, where the view takes in all of Trichy, Srirangam island with its towering gopurams, and the Rock Fort bridge over the Kaveri. Vinayaka Chaturthi is celebrated here with great pomp. The Rockfort is about 3 km from Trichy Junction and 12 km from the airport; December to March is the best time to climb.

places.summary: One of the world's largest working temple complexes — 21 towers on a Kaveri island, 12 km from Trichy.
places.seoDescription: Srirangam: Vishnu's Ranganathaswamy Temple, foremost of the 108 Divya Desams — 63 hectares, 21 towers, a 73 m rajagopuram. 12 km from Trichy.

overview.text:
The Ranganathaswamy Temple at Srirangam is one of the largest functioning religious complexes in the world. Dedicated to Ranganathar, a form of Vishnu, it is the foremost of the 108 Divya Desams sacred to Vaishnavas, and it stands on an island between the Kollidam and Kaveri rivers, about 12 km north of Tiruchirappalli.

It is less a building than a town: the temple and its streets cover 63 hectares in seven concentric enclosures, with 81 shrines, 21 towers and 39 pavilions. The outer rajagopuram, about 73 m tall, was finished only in 1987. The temple's great 21-day festival in the Tamil month of Margazhi (December–January) draws about a million visitors. It is on UNESCO's tentative list. Allow at least half a day.

places.name: Thillai Nataraja Temple, Chidambaram
places.summary: Shiva as the cosmic dancer — the great Chola-era temple of Chidambaram, carved with all 108 dance poses.
places.seoDescription: Chidambaram's Nataraja Temple: Shiva as lord of dance, all 108 karanas carved on its walls, the Natyanjali festival. 220 km south of Chennai.

overview.text:
The Thillai Nataraja Temple at Chidambaram is dedicated to Shiva as Nataraja, the lord of dance, and in Tamil Shaivism it is known simply as Kovil, the temple. Here Shiva is shown performing the Ananda Tandava, the dance of delight, in the golden hall at the heart of the shrine.

The link with dance runs through the whole temple. Its walls are carved with all 108 karanas — the postures described in the Natya Shastra — which form a foundation of Bharatanatyam, and every Maha Shivaratri the Natyanjali dance festival brings performers here. The complex covers 16 hectares, with tall gopurams and a large sacred tank. Chidambaram is about 220 km south of Chennai; the closest airport is about 60 km north at Puducherry.

overview.text:
Velankanni, on the coast 12 km from Nagapattinam, is one of the most famous Christian pilgrim destinations in India. Its heart is the Basilica of Our Lady of Good Health, a white church that draws believers from all over South India and far beyond, and millions of people come every year, for pilgrimage and for leisure.

It is also a beach town, with markets and churches lining the road down to the sea, and it has a long history: Velankanni was once an important port. Come between December and February for the best weather, though pilgrims arrive all year. Nagapattinam station is about 12 km away, and Tiruchirappalli airport about 153 km; regular buses link Velankanni with Trichy, Thanjavur, Chennai, Madurai and Puducherry.

places.summary: An old Danish trading town on the Bay of Bengal — Fort Dansborg, colonial lanes and quiet beaches.
places.seoDescription: Tharangambadi: the old Danish town of Tranquebar — Fort Dansborg museum, New Jerusalem Church, quiet beaches. Best October–February.

overview.text:
Tharangambadi — Tranquebar to the Danes who ruled it — is a small coastal town in Nagapattinam district with an unusual past. In the 17th century it was a busy port, and it became a Danish colony; their great work, Fort Dansborg, still stands by the sea and has been turned into a museum, with ramparts and bastions to walk and views over the Bay of Bengal.

The Danes also built the New Jerusalem Church, one of the oldest Protestant churches in India. Wander the narrow lanes of old houses, then head to the quiet beaches for sunset. The town's seafood is a must-try. Nagapattinam station is about 33 km away, with regular buses; October to February is the best season.

overview.text:
Gingee Fort spreads across three rocky hills in Villupuram district, its walls looping from summit to summit. Once considered impregnable, it was a prize fought over for centuries — by the Cholas and the Marathas, the Mughals and the British — and it is now recognised as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Inside the walls are the ruins of palaces and temples carved with gods and goddesses, watchtowers, and underground tunnels and secret passages once used to escape a siege. The climbs are steep but the views over the green hills and plains are superb; start early to avoid the heat. The fort is about 3 km from Gingee bus stand, 40 km from Villupuram Junction and 160 km from Chennai airport. December to March is the best time.

places.name: Vellore Fort
places.summary: A 16th-century granite fort with a wide moat, a temple, church and mosque inside, and a museum.
places.seoDescription: Vellore Fort: 16th-century Vijayanagara granite fort with a moat, the Jalagandeeswarar Temple and a museum. Open 8 am–6 pm; entry Rs 5.

overview.text:
Vellore Fort is one of the finest examples of military architecture in South India. Vijayanagara chieftains built it in the 16th century from granite quarried nearby, and it covers 133 acres behind a huge moat. It changed hands many times — the Adil Shahis of Bijapur, the Marathas, Daud Khan of Delhi — until the British took it in 1768 and held it until independence; under them, Tipu Sultan's family and Vikrama Rajasinha, the last king of Sri Lanka, were imprisoned here.

Inside the walls stand a mosque, a church and a temple side by side, along with palaces and a government museum. The Jalagandeeswarar Temple is famous for its sculpture. The fort is open from 8 am to 6 pm, and the museum from 9 am to 12.30 pm and 2 to 5 pm, except public holidays. Entry is Rs 5.

overview.text:
Hogenakkal sits on the Kaveri where it crosses from Karnataka into Tamil Nadu's Dharmapuri district. Its name means 'smoky rocks' in Kannada, and it fits: the river splits into countless streams that pour over the dark rock, throwing up spray like smoke, before turning into a white, frothing current.

The classic experience is a ride in a round coracle, drifting gently on the river beneath the falls and through the rocky channels. Downstream, the water flows on into the Mettur reservoir. Hogenakkal is good in every season, but October to February shows the falls in their full glory. Dharmapuri station is about 48 km away and Salem airport about 80 km; buses run from Dharmapuri and Krishnagiri.

places.name: Courtallam (Kutralam) Falls
places.summary: Nine waterfalls in the Western Ghats near Tenkasi — bathe under the 60 m Main Falls.
places.seoDescription: Courtallam: nine falls near Tenkasi — the 60 m Main Falls, Five Falls, Honey Falls, Tiger Falls. Tenkasi station 15 km.

overview.text:
Courtallam — also spelled Coutrallam or Kutralam — is a cluster of nine waterfalls in the Western Ghats near Tenkasi, each with its own height and flow. People come to bathe under them as much as to look: the Main Falls (Peraruvi) drop 60 m, and their water is believed to have healing powers.

A flight of steps from the Main Falls leads to the Small Falls. Honey Falls, 4 km away, is the prettiest; Five Falls spreads out in five streams; Tiger Falls is the best for families with children; and the Shenbaga Falls, reached by an uphill walk, has a temple nearby. Tenkasi station is about 15 km away. Tamil Nadu Tourism lists July, September to November and January to March as the best months.

places.name: Padmanabhapuram Palace
places.summary: The old Travancore royal palace — one of Asia's largest in wood, near Nagercoil; closed Mondays.
places.seoDescription: Padmanabhapuram Palace: Travancore's wooden palace from 1601, 6.5 acres and 15 buildings. Open 9–12.30 and 2–4.30; closed Mondays.

overview.text:
Padmanabhapuram Palace, in Kanyakumari district, was the seat of the old kingdom of Travancore and is one of the largest wooden palaces in Asia. Its core, the Kalkulathu Koikkal, was built in 1601 by Iravi Varma Kulasekhara Perumal; much of the rest dates from the reign of Marthanda Varma, who dedicated the palace to Lord Padmanabha.

The complex covers 6.5 acres and holds 15 buildings, every one rich in intricate woodwork, in the traditional Kerala style. Though it stands in Tamil Nadu, the palace is owned and run by the Government of Kerala as a museum. It is open from 9 am to 12.30 pm and 2 to 4.30 pm, and closed on Mondays. Nagercoil station is about 17 km away and Trivandrum airport about 52 km.

places.name: Thanumalayan Temple, Suchindram
places.summary: A temple to Shiva, Vishnu and Brahma together, with a 44 m gopuram and musical stone pillars, near Kanyakumari.
places.seoDescription: Suchindram's Thanumalayan Temple: Shiva, Vishnu and Brahma in one shrine, a 44 m gopuram, musical pillars. 3.8 km from Nagercoil.

overview.text:
The Thanumalayan Temple at Suchindram, in Kanyakumari district, is unusual among South Indian temples: it is dedicated to the trinity of Shiva, Vishnu and Brahma together. Its first structure was built around the 9th century, and it was later expanded by Thirumalai Nayak and the kings of Travancore, so its architecture mixes Kerala and Tamil styles.

The eastern gopuram rises 11 storeys to 44 m, and the complex holds 30 shrines across about 2 acres. Look for the four musical pillars, each carved from a single stone, and the dancing hall with 1,035 intricately carved pillars. Nagercoil Junction is only about 3.8 km away, so the temple pairs easily with a trip to Kanyakumari. October to March is the best time.

places.name: Arunachaleswarar Temple, Tiruvannamalai
places.summary: Shiva's great temple beneath Arunachala hill, where a giant lamp is lit for Karthigai Deepam.
places.seoDescription: Tiruvannamalai's Arunachaleswarar (Annamalaiyar) Temple: Chola roots, the Karthigai Deepam lamp on the hill. 2 km from the station.

overview.text:
The Arunachaleswarar — or Annamalaiyar — Temple lies at the foot of Arunachala hill in the town of Tiruvannamalai, and is one of the great Shiva temples of Tamil Nadu. At its heart is the Annamalaiyar lingam. Its history reaches back to the Cholas of the 9th century, and the Vijayanagara rulers and the Nayaks later added to it, giving it a blend of Dravidian, Chola and Vijayanagara styles.

The temple's greatest night is Karthigai Deepam, held each year in the Tamil month of Karthigai, when an enormous lamp is lit on top of the hill — a sight that stays with everyone who sees it. Tiruvannamalai station is about 2 km away and Chennai airport about 180 km. November to March is the best time.

places.name: Palani Murugan Temple
places.summary: Lord Murugan's hilltop temple at Palani — climb the steps or take the winch; Thai Poosam is its great festival.
places.seoDescription: Palani: Murugan's hilltop temple on Sivagiri — steps, elephant path, winch and ropeway. Open 6 am–8 pm; Thai Poosam in Jan–Feb.

overview.text:
The Arulmigu Dhandayuthapani Swamy Temple crowns Sivagiri, the higher of Palani's two hills in Dindigul district, and is one of the richest temples in India. Its idol of Lord Murugan is made of navapashanam, a mix of nine herbal substances, attributed to the siddhar Bogar.

Pilgrims reach the top by climbing the steps, by the gentler elephant path, or by winch and ropeway. Many carry kavadi on their shoulders, and tonsuring is an important tradition. The temple is open from 6 am to 8 pm (from 4.30 am on festival days); the winch runs from 7 am to 12.30 pm and 1.30 to 5 pm. Thai Poosam, in January–February, is the biggest festival. Palani station is about 2 km away and Coimbatore airport about 114 km.

places.name: Yercaud
places.summary: A small hill station in the Shevaroy hills above Salem — a boating lake, orchids and viewpoints.
places.seoDescription: Yercaud: hill station in the Shevaroys, 28 km from Salem — the lake, Orchidarium, Lady's Seat, Pagoda Point; summer festival in May.

overview.text:
Yercaud is a compact, easygoing hill station in the Shevaroy hills, a 28 km drive up from Salem. Its name comes from the Tamil words for lake and forest, and those are still its pleasures: a placid lake for boating at the centre of town, and wooded slopes full of coffee estates and fruit orchards — the hills grow coffee, oranges, jackfruit, guava, black pepper and cardamom.

Start at the botanical garden and the Orchidarium of the Botanical Survey of India, then take a boat out on the lake. Beyond town are viewpoints such as Lady's Seat and Pagoda Point, Anna Park with its flower show, the Shevaroy temple, Bear's Cave and Kiliyur Falls. The summer festival is held in May. Salem Junction is about 35 km away, and the season runs from October to June.

places.name: Pagoda Point
places.summary: Yercaud's eastern viewpoint over Salem and the 21 hairpin bends.
places.seoDescription: Pagoda Point: Yercaud's viewpoint over Salem, Kakambadi and the 21 hairpin bends.

overview.text: Pagoda Point, on the eastern edge of the Yercaud hills, gives a bird's-eye view of the whole town of Salem, the village of Kakambadi and the 21 hairpin bends of the ghat road. It is also called Pyramid Point, after four piles of stones arranged like a pyramid that resemble a temple tower, and there is an old Rama temple nearby.

places.name: Kolli Hills
places.summary: Untamed hills at 1,000–1,300 m — 1,000 steps down to Agaya Gangai falls, Siddhar caves and tribal villages.
places.seoDescription: Kolli Hills: 1,000–1,300 m, Agaya Gangai falls down 1,000 steps, Siddhar caves, Selur viewpoint. 88 km from Salem Junction.

overview.text:
The Kolli Hills, in Namakkal district, rise to 1,000–1,300 m and enjoy pleasant weather all year round. They have an untamed feel, far from the busier hill stations, and you can get to know the village life of the tribal hamlets here.

The must-see is Agaya Gangai — also called the Kollimalai falls — reached by descending 1,000 steps; trekkers love the trail. Near the falls are the caves of the siddhars Bogar and Agastya, while others lie deep in the forest, 2–3 hours of steep trekking away. There is boating on Vasalurpatty lake, and the road to the Selur viewpoint, one of the highest points, runs through plantations and orange trees. Salem Junction is about 88 km away and Trichy airport about 133 km; June to October is recommended.
